question: France has adopted Law No 2023-659 of 26 July 2023 to combat social dumping by shipping companies using flags of convenience on cross-Channel transport. The law stipulates that the French minimum wage must apply for the crew of all shipping companies, irrespective of the flag they fly, with regular international passenger crossings docking at a French port. In addition, crew must be given at least as many days of rest on land as they have days of service on board. 1.

While the Commission is looking into whether this national law is in line with EU law, particularly in regard to the provisions of Article 9(1) of Regulation (EC) No 593/2008 (Rome I), can it clarify its approach in substance regarding this important issue?
Does the Commission intend to apply a similar measure at EU level in order to combat social dumping effectively, protect workers’ rights and avoid any risk of fragmentation of the internal market?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.1.2025) 1. The Commission is aware of the French legislation that entered into force in June 2024 (Law No 2023-659) and is in constant communication with the French authorities to discuss legal and practical implications of this legislation for France and other Member States. 2. The Commission recognises the importance of the protection of seafarers’ rights.

Most of the Maritime Labour Convention1 has been incorporated in the EU legislation2. The EU and its Member States are also actively involved in negotiations on further improving the working and living conditions of seafarers in the context of amendments to the Code of the Maritime Labour Convention.

Moreover, seafarers are covered by several acts of the EU labor legislation which include, among others, protection in the event of insolvency of their employer, and establishment of a general framework for informing and consulting employees in the EU.

The Commission is ready to assess ways to further improve working conditions and social protection for seafarers in the EU, also considering the protection of the integrity of the internal market and the competitiveness of the shipping industry. The Commission will hold consultations with maritime administrations of the Member States and stakeholders on the way forward.
